body.text: The Civil Rights Board implements the general policy and purposes set forth in Chapter 18 "Non-Discrimination" and Chapter 18A "Fair Housing" of the City of Kalamazoo Code of Ordinances. The Board was created in September 2020 following updates to Chapter 18.

The Board fosters mutual understanding and respect among the people in the City, working to discourage and prevent unlawful discriminatory practices toward the protected classes described in the Ordinance.
Board meetings are conducted under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, and Board records are available to the public under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act.

items: Review claims of discrimination brought by City residents and make recommendations for resolution, following investigation of the claim by the City Manager or the City Manager's designee.
Review and analyze conditions, practices, attitudes, policies and other factors within Kalamazoo that contribute to discriminatory impact and further inequities.
Evaluate the impact of antidiscrimination efforts.
Make recommendations to the City Commission and City Manager on ways to improve City programs and ordinances to eliminate discrimination.
Make recommendations on ways to remove the effects of past discrimination.
Establish bylaws and procedural rules for its meetings, subject to approval by the City Commission.
Provide an annual report to the City Commission on complaints received and actions taken.
Under the bylaws, the Chairperson sees that the annual report is submitted by February 1 each year.
Foster mutual understanding and respect among the people in the City, and discourage and prevent unlawful discriminatory practices toward the protected classes described in the Ordinance.
Engage in public awareness activities so residents are informed of local protections and the role of the Board.
Engage with federal, state and local agencies to assist in addressing issues of discrimination in the City.

body.text: The Board reviews claims and makes recommendations. Investigation of a claim is carried out by the City Manager or the City Manager's designee, not by the Board.
The Board consists of 9 members: 7 voting members and 2 ex-officio members who have no vote but may otherwise fully participate in any meeting.

body.label: Appointment
body.value: Voting members are appointed by the Mayor and approved by the City Commission.

body.label: Expertise Required
body.value: Members must be able to demonstrate experience in civil rights, public accommodation, employment, disability or housing law.

body.label: Residency
body.value: Members shall be residents of the City, reflecting and representing the diversity of the Kalamazoo community. Up to 2 members may be non-residents when there is a valid reason, such as working in the City or holding special expertise needed to carry out the Board's duties.

body.label: Ex-Officio Members
body.value: One City Commissioner, and one City officer or employee recommended by the City Manager who is neither a City Commissioner nor the City Manager. Both are appointed by the Mayor and approved by the City Commission.

body.label: Term Length
body.value: Three years. Members may serve up to two consecutive terms. A member whose term has expired may continue to serve until a successor is appointed.

body.label: Attendance
body.value: A member absent for 3 consecutive meetings, or for more than 50% of regular meetings over a six-month period, is considered to have resigned and the seat is deemed vacant.

body.label: Quorum
body.value: Five members. Ex-officio members count toward establishing a quorum.

appealProcess.title: How complaints work
appealProcess.intro: Five steps run from the complaint to the Board's recommendation. The first two are yours, and the complaint carries a deadline.

steps.title: Gather your information
steps.desc: Before filing, collect what happened and when, and the person or organization the complaint is about. It also helps to note whether you have already referred the complaint elsewhere, such as the Fair Housing Center of Southwest Michigan or the Michigan Department of Civil Rights.

steps.title: File the complaint
steps.desc: File online, or bring the paper form to City Hall during business hours, or mail it to the City Manager's Office at 241 W South Street. The incident must have happened inside Kalamazoo city limits and within the last 91 days, or it cannot be investigated. Complaints that fall outside the City's ordinance are referred to the appropriate authority.

steps.title: The City confirms receipt
steps.desc: A member of the City's team follows up within three business days to confirm your complaint was received. If you filed online, you are also notified once the appropriate staff have reviewed it whether it will be investigated.

steps.title: The investigation
steps.desc: The complaint is investigated by City staff with relevant knowledge and experience, under the City Manager or the City Manager's designee. The Board does not investigate. The results of the investigation are shared with the Board.

steps.title: The Board's recommendation
steps.desc: The Board reviews the claim and the investigation results. If the ordinance was violated, the Board makes a recommendation to the City Manager on how it should be addressed. The Board recommends; it does not decide or enforce.

items: The incident must have happened within Kalamazoo city limits.
Complaints more than 91 days after the incident cannot be investigated.
Complaints become public information and may be discussed by the Civil Rights Board or released under a Freedom of Information Act request. The City says it uses discretion when responding.
Local protections go beyond state and federal law, covering source of income, status as a survivor of domestic violence, and prior arrest or conviction record.
